summary: Nimbus's order book is growing faster than its revenue, and the market price implies slower growth than the evidence supports. The thesis holds while backlog keeps converting and margins stay intact.

facts.text: Revenue rose to $1.25 billion in the June 2026 quarter from $980 million a year earlier, up 27.6% [m:revenue:2026-06-30] [m:revenue:2025-06-30].
Remaining performance obligations reached $4.2 billion, 44.8% above a year earlier [m:rpo:2026-06-30] [m:rpo:2025-06-30].
Management expects fiscal 2027 capital expenditures of approximately $1.8 billion [f:6f1c2a52-3b1e-4c43-9e59-3d1b1f0a0001].
A hyperscale cloud provider placed a $600 million multi-year order [f:6f1c2a52-3b1e-4c43-9e59-3d1b1f0a0002].
The order-book signal S1 fired with strength 0.82 [s:S1].

why_mispriced.text: The price implies 12% annual growth, below the 18% the evidence supports [c:C2].

inferences: Inference: the order book growing faster than revenue suggests revenue growth can continue if orders convert on the usual schedule.
assumptions: Assumption: backlog converts to revenue within 24 months (assumed).
Assumption: the operating margin stays above 15% (assumed).

risks.text: Customer concentration: one hyperscaler placed the largest disclosed order [f:6f1c2a52-3b1e-4c43-9e59-3d1b1f0a0002].
Heavy capital spending could strain free cash flow [f:6f1c2a52-3b1e-4c43-9e59-3d1b1f0a0001].

kill_criteria.why: The thesis rests on the order book growing; under 10% a year it no longer leads revenue.
Growth bought with falling margins is not the thesis.
